description: ODC (coverage C): SWITCH and ON EXCEPTION, three types that had never passed through the ODC lane, in the raw verbs so that the interface names stay in the job itself. (1) ISwitchNode and ISwitchCondition: the Switch is an action node like the If, but the branches are not properties: each branch IS an ISwitchCondition, which is already the connector itself (IActionConnector), so the `link` of a condition uses the default connector Target and there is no connector named after the case. The Otherwise branch, that one yes, is the property OtherwiseTarget of the node, and it is MANDATORY: without it Verify returns InvalidFlow_NoOtherwise. (2) IOnExceptionAction: the global UI handler, which is a child of a UI FLOW (IUIFlow.CreateOnExceptionHandler) and not of the eSpace, has no IStartNode (each IExceptionHandlerNode is a start) and is the only place, along with ISystemEvent, where an IMessageNode is allowed. Because it has no Start, a handler does not accept `layout` either (FlowLayout requires a Start): positions are set by hand, with move x/y. IESpace.GlobalExceptionHandler is deliberately NOT touched: the property is writable, but re-pointing the global handler of an app that already has one costs three new warnings (AllExceptionsInNonGlobalFlow on the flow that lost its post and NoErrorHandlingForAllExceptions on each flow that was left uncovered), that is, breaking the error handling of the fixture.

ops._why: deliberately with name: in If, Assign, ForEach and Switch the name of the create is discarded by the runtime; what shows up in the flow is the Label, proven by the get at the end
ISwitchCondition is not born from a CreateNode: the kernel finds ISwitchNode.CreateCondition() by itself, which takes no name
Value is a boolean ExpressionProperty: OutSystems text, only functions from docs/functions.md
the condition IS the connector (ISwitchCondition : IActionConnector, writable Target), so it links through the default connector Target; there is no connector called Case1 on the Switch
the Otherwise is the ONLY output of the Switch that is a property (IActionNode OtherwiseTarget {get;set;}), and it is mandatory: without it Verify returns Error InvalidFlow_NoOtherwise

the evaluation order of the cases is the order of the CONNECTORS, not that of the declaration; these two moves are literally what the LogicExpander emits at the end of each switch to restore the written order
